recipes.name: Party Mimosa
ingredients_raw: 1 (6 ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed and undiluted

steps.text: Stir together apricot nectar, pineapple juice, water, and orange juice concentrate in a large pitcher until combined. Pour in bottle of sparkling wine just before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Party Mimosa
raw_recipe.description: This tropical fruit mimosa is a wonderful change, and will serve several people too!
raw_recipe.name: Party Mimosa
recipeIngredient: 1 (6 ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed and undiluted

recipeInstructions.text: Stir together apricot nectar, pineapple juice, water, and orange juice concentrate in a large pitcher until combined. Pour in bottle of sparkling wine just before serving.

review.reviewBody: I made this for a brunch and everyone loved it. I used apricot nectar since I couldn't find apricot-mango, but followed the rest of the recipe. I like this recipe better than the traditional orange juice-champagne combination. I has more flavor. I used a cheap bottle of champagne ($5.99 a bottle) but no one noticed. I put a couple of fresh raspberries in the bottom of the glasses before adding the juice and champagne. It looked beautiful!

Love! I do not premix with champagne since it works great with Sprite or 7up as well. I've made for kids (or adults) and simply put the 'bubbly' part in a cup first, then add the juice mix to it accordingly. Always a party fav! I use any kind of nectar (guava, mango, apricot-mango, strawberry, etc) and they all work well. Without premixing the 'bubbly' part, all can enjoy however they prefer it mixed.

Very good, just the right amount of sweetness and citrus. I used the apricot, mango nectars. I mixed a 12 oz can of frozen OJ with 3 cans of water. I used prosecco and let guests add they amount they wanted to their glass. Froze ice cubes of cranberry juice for color.

I served this at a July 4th Brunch and everyone raved about how good it was. Like most of the reviewers, I could not find the Apricot-Mango nectar but was able to find a bottle of Apricot Nectar and a bottle of Mango Nectar at my local grocery store, so I mixed the two but found that it needed a little more Mango Nectar than Apricot. I also added a couple shots of Orange Liqueur (Grand Marnier) to take something that's 'over the top' to 'out of this world' I also froze a batch without the alcohol in an ice tray and used the cubes to keep the pitcher cold without diluting it.

This recipe was great with our breakfast casserole! I always thought a mimosa was just OJ + champagne, so when I read this, it peaked my interest. Unfortunately, my grocery store didn't have the apricot-mango nector. Fortunately, I found Mango Pineapple juice, so I used 24 ounces of that, and it tasted great! I also read that a reviewer put raspberries in hers, so I plopped 2 raspberries in each of my crystal glasses...it was pretty. :) I will definitely make this again when I want to have a fancy breakfast!

This was yummy for Mother's Day brunch today. Used 1 can (12oz) each Jumex brand Apricot nectar and Mango nectar, along with the Pineapple and OJ concentrate. Mixed that up in a pitcher and filled flutes halfway up and then added Asti Spumanti or Sprite for each person. Served 8 and they wish they had more!

This mimosa was the hit of my Mother's Day bash! I couldn't find the ingredients exactly, though, so mine was a little different. I used pineapple/mango juice, frozen oj, and champagne. I also made a frozen ring out of the pineapple/mango juice, cut up strawberries and kiwis. Everyone loved it!
I quadrupled the recipe for all the juices and made in one pitcher, then let everyone add their own champagne. Float a few raspberries in the glass and this was a hit!!!!

This was great. I made a Bellini bar and had this in a pitcher with bottles of prosecco for guests to make their own Bellini. Went over really great. Everyone loved it. Chef at French restaurant asked me for recipe. I couldn't find the mango apricot so I used peach nectar, mango nectar, pineapple juice and concentrated oj. No water. I put frozen strawberries in the pitcher to keep it cold.

Made a pitcher of this on Christmas. As most reviewers commented, could not find the combo of apricot/mango nectar, so purchased 2 cans of Kern nectar and a bottle of mango nectar (from Trader Joes). We doubled the recipe (wo/champagne)- and set it out for either kids to enjoy alone or adults w/champagne or vodka- wish we had made more! It was all gone before the guests were gone!

If I cannot find the apricot-mango nectar I just use 6 ounces of apricot nectar and 6 ounces of mango nectar which are easily found in the Goya section of the grocery store. I use a good asti since I am not a fan of dry champagne and it comes out perfect. There is never any mimosa discarded down the drain!
Big hit for New Years Eve. Couldn't find apricot-mango nectar. Used 1/2 mango and 1/2 peach nectar. put 2-3 raspberries in glass
Too sweet for my tastes. Maybe pour in two bottles of champagne next time.

...we had this for easter, and it was simply delicious...we actually ran out of it before any other beverage served...we're having it again this morning for mother's day because this mama loved it...lol...
Love this variation! Great balance of sweet and tart.
Served this at a post holiday brunch for friends... Perfect!
I made it with Peach Mango rather than Apricot Mango and it was a big hit! Party Mimosa may very well become part of our holiday tradition. Thank you!
We love this recipe! Thanks for sharing! I am digging it out to make for New Years Day brunch. Everyone who tries it really likes it! Happy New Year!
This was my Easter Brunch Beverage The Ladies Loved It!

I couldn't find apricot-mango nectar so I just used apricot nectar. Great with champagne or ginger ale for the kids and non-drinkers. I made a pitcher of the juice and then poured mimosas to order instead of pouring the champagne directly into the pitcher of juice.
